methodology.headline: How we verify before we publish
methodology.lede: Every claim is anchored in statutory releases, triangulated against Controller of Budget and Auditor-General records, then framed for newsrooms and citizens.

steps.title: Ingest & Trace
steps.subtitle: PFM Act & Constitution (Art. 201-207)
steps.description: We track statutory releases against the budget calendar - Budget Policy Statements (BPS), County Fiscal Strategy Papers (CFSP), and Appropriation Bills.
steps.highlight: No speculative commentary; anchored in official government gazettes.

steps.title: Triangulate & Verify
steps.subtitle: Controller of Budget & OAG Records
steps.description: Every Treasury and county allocation is cross-verified against actual Controller of Budget (CoB) exchequer withdrawals and Auditor-General audit findings.
steps.highlight: Zero published claims without primary documentation backing.

steps.title: Frame & Publish
steps.subtitle: Feed-Ready Dashboards & Newsroom Packs
steps.description: We translate complex public finance spreadsheets into actionable scorecards, interactive dashboards, and investigative media toolkits.
steps.highlight: Published in English, Kiswahili, and Sheng for maximum civic reach.

steps.title: Convene & Hold Pressure
steps.subtitle: Multi-Camera Town Halls & Briefings
steps.description: We convene facilitated citizen-official forums and provide embargoed briefings to newsroom editors ahead of critical fiscal votes.
steps.highlight: Turning verified evidence into structured, non-partisan public dialogue.

items.name: BNS Connect
items.headline: The budget lands as a PDF. We break it down for the Locals.
items.body: Every June, Kenya debates a national budget measured in trillions. By July, most of that debate has left the public conversation. BNS Connect is the year-round programme that picks up Treasury releases, verify claims against published documents, and publish what holds up - dashboards, briefing products, and story series partners and institutions can use. .
items.highlight: FY2026/27 national budget: about KSh 4.8 trillion, drawn from published Treasury figures - the scale Connect exists to watch.
items.investorThesis: Trillions are debated for 48 hours in June, then disbursed and spent in silence for the other eleven months.
items.whatWeDo: We track Kenya's KSh 4.8T national budget from Treasury allocation through ministry execution - verifying statutory releases against Controller of Budget records and publishing actionable intelligence for institutions and newsrooms.
items.mandateFit: Macro-Fiscal Governance · Sovereign Debt Accountability · Youth Civic Technology

process.title: Follow the allocation
process.body: Trackers pick up each Treasury release and trace the line from national allocation to the ministry or agency meant to spend it.

process.title: Verify on the ground
process.body: Claims are checked against documents and lived experience - nothing publishes on vibes. Verified findings only.

process.title: Publish for the feed
process.body: Findings ship as dashboards, story series, and social threads in English, Kiswahili, and Sheng - built for sharing.

process.title: Keep scrutiny alive
process.body: Quarterly briefs and the annual survey keep pressure on all year, not just on Budget Day.

items.name: BNS Mashinani
items.headline: Kakamega. Kilifi. Nakuru. Wajir. Grassroots agents.
items.body: BNS Mashinani chooses depth: embedded teams in four counties - Kakamega, Kilifi, Nakuru, and Wajir - present for the full budget cycle. We work alongside county governments as accountability partners, not adversaries, and turn what we find into public scorecards, live trackers, and Promise versus Delivery stories rooted in places people actually live.
items.highlight: Four counties. Full-cycle presence. A model built to be copied - not a thin tour of forty-seven.
items.investorThesis: Devolution sent KSh 400B+ to counties, but oversight remained fly-over workshops with zero longitudinal ground truth.
items.whatWeDo: Embedded teams in Kakamega, Kilifi, Nakuru, and Wajir track the complete 12-month budget cycle as constructive accountability partners, verifying whether allocated capital actually delivered functional clinics, classrooms, and water infrastructure.
items.mandateFit: Sub-National Governance · Devolution Delivery · Public Participation (Art. 196/201)

deliverables.title: Quarterly County Budget Scorecards
deliverables.description: Rigorous public evaluations grading own-source revenue mobilization and development expenditure execution.

deliverables.title: Promise vs. Delivery Field Dossiers
deliverables.description: On-the-ground investigative verifications matching approved procurement budgets against functional physical assets.

deliverables.title: Facilitated Multi-Camera Town Halls
deliverables.description: Documented community-official forums that bring county executives, assembly members, and residents together.

pillars.title: Embedded county teams
pillars.body: Teams present in Kakamega, Kilifi, Nakuru, and Wajir for the full budget cycle - not single site visits - working as accountability partners, not adversaries.

pillars.title: County scorecards
pillars.body: Revenue versus development execution, graded in public scorecards that carry real weight with county governments.

pillars.title: Promise vs. Delivery
pillars.body: Stories that match what was pledged against what was delivered - plus authentic stories celebrating strides these counties have made.

process.title: Embed, don't visit
process.body: Teams settle into the four counties and stay for the whole cycle, building trust with officials and residents alike.

process.title: Track the cycle
process.body: From county fiscal strategy papers to approved budgets to execution reports - every stage is monitored and documented.

process.title: Score in public
process.body: Findings convert into scorecards and live trackers that counties can respond to and citizens can use.

process.title: Convene the forum
process.body: Town halls bring officials and residents into the same room, with BNS facilitation and multi-camera documentation.

faqs.a: Kakamega, Kilifi, Nakuru, and Wajir - four diverse counties chosen to build a replicable full-cycle model for the other 43.

faqs.q: Why only four counties instead of all 47?
faqs.a: Covering all 47 produces thin data and little accountability. Depth in four counties creates a model with real weight - and a template others can copy.

faqs.q: How do counties work with BNS?
faqs.a: As accountability partners. BNS teams work alongside county governments through the full cycle, pairing scrutiny with recognition of genuine progress.

items.name: Wanahabari Lab
items.headline: Budget Day isn't one day, We capture all reportings year round.
items.body: Kenyan newsrooms still treat the Cabinet Secretary's briefcase as the climax of the fiscal year. Wanahabari Lab is built for what comes next.  At Wanahabari lab,  we train and report  on public finance.
items.highlight: Four Labs a year. Roughly one hundred and twenty to two hundred journalists and creators trained annually.
items.investorThesis: Kenyan newsrooms treat Budget Day as a 1-day political circus, leaving the remaining 364 days of expenditure uninvestigated.
items.whatWeDo: We train mainstream reporters and digital creators side-by-side on live fiscal evidence, anchoring one-day intensives to statutory milestones so cohorts leave with filed investigations, forensic media toolkits, and membership in an active alumni press bench.
items.mandateFit: Investigative Journalism · Public Interest Media · Counter-Disinformation

process.title: Pick the fiscal moment
process.body: Each quarter, the Lab anchors to what is actually happening - budget estimates, approvals, Coffee Bill debates, audit releases.

process.title: Train on live evidence
process.body: Sessions run on real BNS data and documents, with facilitators who track the numbers daily.

process.title: File the story
process.body: Participants produce publishable budget stories during the Lab itself - with editorial support on accuracy.

faqs.q: Who can apply for Wanahabari Lab?
faqs.a: Mainstream journalists, reporters, newsroom editors, and digital creators across Kenya who cover governance, public finance, policy, or community affairs.
Quarterly - four one-day Labs a year, each anchored to a real moment in the fiscal calendar. Applications open quarterly.
Publishable stories filed during the Lab, plus a full media toolkit: data, contacts, explainers, and story angles for their outlet or platform.

items.name: BNS Studios
items.headline: High-craft media. A civic surplus attached.
items.body: If your impact story only lives in a grant PDF, it never reaches the people who need it. BNS Studios is the production house that turns institutional evidence into podcasts, documentaries, explainers, animations, social series, and facilitated town halls - for governments meeting public participation duties, development partners chasing localisation goals, companies delivering serious commercial work, and CSOs without an in-house crew. We are mission-aligned and editorially independent. A portion of Studios surplus funds Budget Ndio Story's civic work, so every commission carries a second job: keeping public-finance literacy alive beyond the client brief.
items.highlight: Commission once: your audience gets the film or forum; civic programmes get sustained fuel from the surplus.
items.investorThesis: Impact research trapped in dry 100-page PDFs generates zero political cost or citizen engagement.
items.whatWeDo: BNS Studios is the self-sustaining commercial-grade production house turning institutional evidence into cinema-grade documentaries, animated explainers, podcasts, and facilitated town halls - with production surplus directly funding BNS civic programmes.
